incident-bot: :rotating_light: SLO breach detected: p99 latency >= 1.8s for route /v1/generate (us-east-1). Spike started at 2026-03-15T02:40:32Z. Affected model: redwood-instruct (quant profile: int8-v2-quick). Streaming stalls and tail jitter observed. Paging @maya (oncall).

maya (oncall): Ack. I'm on it. Any known rollouts in the last 6-12 hours?

liam (eng-runtime): There was an automated calibration rollout for int8-v2-quick at ~2026-03-15T00:55Z to canary, promoted to prod at ~01:30Z. It changed per-layer quant thresholds and KV cache hot-slot handling (reduced cached value lifespan).

jordan (eng-sre): Observing p95 up from 220ms -> 680ms, p99 from 490ms -> 1.9s. Streaming stall rate increased (client-side timeouts) and number of active reorders up. Here's a quick log sample (tail):

```
2026-03-15T02:39:58Z node=serving-12 model=redwood-instruct profile=int8-v2-quick seq_len=1536 kv_evictions=12 dequant_recompute_ms=420
2026-03-15T02:40:04Z node=serving-03 model=redwood-instruct profile=int8-v2-quick stream_stall=true stall_duration_ms=820
2026-03-15T02:40:12Z node=serving-07 model=redwood-instruct profile=int8-v2-quick p99_ms=1890
```

liam (eng-runtime): That log matches a pattern we saw in a staging run — the new thresholds cause more frequent KV cache evictions for sequences >1024, which forces repeated dequantization work and stalls streaming `next_token` paths. We didn't hit this pattern in canary because traffic there has shorter context on average.

maya (oncall): Customer impact? Any timed-out requests or error spikes?

eli (cs): CS reporting 4 customers in US-East are seeing intermittent 5xx/timeouts from the ingest side; two have opened tickets complaining about long response times. No widespread errors yet, but UX is degraded for some high-ctx workloads.

jordan (eng-sre): Temporary mitigation options: 1) route production traffic away from int8-v2-quick to safe_profile (int8-v1) or fp16 fallback; 2) increase capacity on redwood-instruct pool to absorb extra compute; 3) enable per-route short-circuit to drop long-sequence streaming requests (not ideal). I'd prefer rollback to int8-v1 for a quick fix.

liam (eng-runtime): Agreed. Rolling profile weights back is fastest. I'm prepping a hot rollback. Command I'll run (monitoring for 5min):

```
rctl profile promote --model redwood-instruct --from int8-v1 --to-prod --reason "hot rollback: streaming stall p99 spike"
# fallback alternative:
rctl routing set-weight --model redwood-instruct --profile int8-v2-quick=0 --profile int8-v1=100
```

maya (oncall): Do it. Also notify the console to enable immediate fallback for streaming paths. I'll open a paging handoff to eng-runtime for ownership.

eng-runtime-bot: Started job r-98321: promote-profile (redwood-instruct) by liam. Estimated propagation about 30-90s per node, global drain/replace to avoid mid-request profile flip.

liam (eng-runtime): Promotion started. Watching p95/p99 in metrics.

(2 minutes pass)

jordan (eng-sre): Early signal: p99 dropped to 740ms, p95 at ~300ms. Stall counts decreasing. Still a few stragglers on older nodes.

eli (cs): Noting customers A and B have their tickets marked "affected by rollback mitigation". I'll push updates and offer extended logs if needed.

maya (oncall): After initial rollback, some nodes still exhibiting high dequant_recompute_ms. liam, can you force a graceful restart of serving nodes that still report int8-v2-quick in their health?

liam (eng-runtime): Yep. Hitting restart group redwood-instruct-prod-3. Command: `rctl node restart --group redwood-instruct-prod-3 --graceful`

(1 minute)

liam (eng-runtime): Restarts completed for group 3. All nodes report profile int8-v1 now.

jordan (eng-sre): Metrics stabilized: p99 ~420ms, p95 ~260ms, stall rate back to baseline. No ongoing SLO breach.

maya (oncall): Great. Incident severity -> monitoring. I'm going to hand off to liam/jordan for follow-up root cause & postmortem. Immediate action items: rollback confirmed, CS notified, customers updated.

sophie (eng-ml): From ML side, int8-v2-quick calibration reduced quant clip thresholds to squeeze latency/cost on short contexts but introduced instability on long-context KV tails. We'll run tuned calibration tests with backpressure for sequences >1024 and add a gating rule to avoid switching perf-sensitive profiles in prod without long-context synthetic load.

liam (eng-runtime): Follow-up tickets created:
- RUNTIME-4123 rollback-postmortem (owner: liam)
- ML-2248 calib-int8-v2-longctx-regression (owner: sophie)
- SRE-3301 add-canary-long-seq-tests (owner: jordan)

maya (oncall): Thanks everyone. Final notes for the log: cause = int8-v2-quick calibration interacting poorly with KV cache eviction policy on long contexts -> dequant thrash -> streaming stalls -> p99 breach. Mitigation = promoted int8-v1 (rollback) + node restarts. Customer impact = 4 affected customers, 2 active tickets, CS notified.

eli (cs): I'll follow up with the two impacted customers and attach timeline. Please cc me on postmortem so I can coordinate any credits or remediation.

maya (oncall): I'll close the page. If anyone sees re-emergence, reopen or escalate. :thumbsup:

liam (eng-runtime): A couple of quick PRs already in draft to add long-context travis-style tests and a sysctl guard for KV eviction thresholds. Will iterate with Sophie and Jordan.

sophie (eng-ml): I'll add synthetic traffic with mixed seq lengths to the canary harness and ensure int8-v2 variants are gated on that pass.

jordan (eng-sre): Marking incident resolved for now, will link timeline to SRE dashboard.

incident-bot: Incident state changed: RESOLVED -> monitoring. Incident created: INC-2026-0315-047 (linked tickets: RUNTIME-4123, ML-2248, SRE-3301).

maya (oncall): Closing thread. Good work team.
